X-stiff.text: This report presents a comprehensive evaluation of open-source alternatives to Jev, a hosted model developed by TypeSafe that provides probabilistic responses to typed questions. The evaluation encompasses seven open-source solutions across 14 configurations executed sequentially on a single 8 GB consumer GPU. Each configuration was assessed utilizing a standardized set of 764 out-of-domain decisions, with Jev evaluated via the TypeSafe API for comparative purposes. The results indicate that Kev-4B, quantized to 4-bit precision, represents the optimal solution, demonstrating a memory footprint of 3.7 GB, a performance differential of 4.7 points relative to Jev at equivalent latency, a reduced incidence of high-confidence errors, and zero per-call cost.

Y-casual.text: So TypeSafe put out Jev, which answers pick-one, yes/no and score questions with probabilities instead of spitting out text. A week later there were seven open-source knockoffs. We grabbed all seven, ran 14 setups one at a time on one 8 GB gaming card, and threw the same 764 questions at each, plus Jev itself over its API. Winner: Kev-4B squashed to 4-bit. It fits in 3.7 GB, ends up 4.7 points behind Jev at the same speed, is confidently wrong less often, and doesn't cost a cent per call.
